Declares MSDataWritingConsumer (one constructor, destructor, four IMSDataConsumer overrides, addDataProcessing, two counters, two private pure virtual hooks, doCleanup_ and eleven protected members) plus PlainMSDataWritingConsumer and NoopMSDataWritingConsumer.

The ported implementation. Source of the whole state machine: the dummy one-record map that produces the header, the manually written list tags carrying the expected counts, the running record index handed to writeSpectrum_/writeChromatogram_, and doCleanup_'s close-list-then-footer order.

source_anchors.operation: class @note: the first consumeChromatogram or consumeSpectrum starts writing the mzML header to disk, together with the first element
class @note: spectra may not be added after chromatograms, because that would put two spectrumList tags in one mzML file
class @note: the expected size is not enforced and a wrong value leaves an inconsistent mzML whose spectrumList/chromatogramList count attribute disagrees with its contents
processSpectrum_ and processChromatogram_ (line 161) are private pure virtuals: the class is abstract and the template-method hooks are the only extension point
PlainMSDataWritingConsumer defines both hooks as empty bodies and nothing else; its constructor forwards the filename
NoopMSDataWritingConsumer still takes a filename and still runs the base constructor, which creates and truncates that file, even though every method and doCleanup_ are overridden to do nothing
the output stream is opened in binary mode so no line-ending conversion happens, and its precision is set to writtenDigits(double())
the destructor calls doCleanup_, so closing the document is tied to object lifetime and cannot report a failure
consumeSpectrum throws Exception::IllegalArgument with "Cannot write spectra after writing chromatograms." when writing_chromatograms_ is set
the record is copied before processing (SpectrumType scpy = s), so the caller's record is never modified by the hook or by the added data processing
the header is written from a dummy map holding the experimental settings plus this one record, so fileContent, sourceFileList and dataProcessingList describe the first record only
the spectrumList tag is written by hand with spectra_expected_ as its count and defaultDataProcessingRef="dp_sp_0", once, when the first spectrum arrives
'// TODO writeSpectrum assumes that dps_ has at least one value -> assert this here ...' - the source's own marker for the unchecked data-processing assumption that streaming creates
writeSpectrum_ receives spectra_written_++ as the record index and renew_native_ids = false, so the record's own native identifier is written through even when empty
consumeChromatogram closes an open spectrumList before doing anything else and clears writing_spectra_
the chromatogramList tag carries chromatograms_expected_ and, like the spectrumList tag, defaultDataProcessingRef="dp_sp_0"
addDataProcessing replaces additional_dataprocessing_ with a new pointer rather than appending, so calling it twice keeps only the second entry
doCleanup_ closes spectrumList, else chromatogramList - never both, which is correct because consumeChromatogram already closed the spectrum list
the footer is written only when started_writing_ is set, so a consumer that received no record leaves an empty file
the spectrum open tag takes its index attribute from the running record number s, which is why a record rendered on its own has to be renumbered

a record with a non-default source file emits sourceFileRef="sf_sp_<s>" from the running index; under this consumer the header declared only the first record's source file, so every later reference is dangling

dataProcessingRef is emitted when s == 0 or the history differs from dps[0], and the search for a matching entry falls back to dp_ref_num = s when none is found; with the one-record dps_ this consumer builds, that fallback names an undeclared element

writeSourceFile_(os, std::string("sf_sp_") + i, ...) with Size i: the only viable operator+ is the charT overload, so the declared id ends in a narrowed character - '\0' for i == 0 - while line 5254 streams the integer. The adjacent run-level call at line 4964 uses StringUtils::toStr(i) correctly

writeDataProcessing_(os, std::string("dp_sp_") + s, ...) with Size s has the same narrowing shape, while the list tags at lines 4784 and 4823 reference the literal "dp_sp_0"; lines 5123 and 5194 repeat the pattern for software and per-array processing ids
renew_native_ids builds std::string("spectrum=") + s from a Size, the same narrowing; not reachable through this consumer, which passes renew_native_ids = false
'#MSDataWritingConsumer_test' - the class test is commented out and never built, which is why ten of its eleven sections are '// TODO' and the eleventh does not compile

evidence: Tier 3 source review plus tier 4 native invariants. The upstream class test contributes no expected value at all - ten '// TODO' sections, one section that cannot compile, and the whole file disabled in executables.cmake - so nothing here is a transcribed C++ literal except the two error message texts and the element/attribute names, which are read from MSDataWritingConsumer.cpp and MzMLHandler.cpp and are tier-3 evidence on that basis. The structural expectations (header at the first record, the list tags carrying the expected counts, the close-list-then-footer order, spectra refused after chromatograms, the record copy, addDataProcessing replacing rather than appending, the counters) are each pinned to a source_anchor above. The strongest independent check is tier 4 and does not depend on the C++ at all: tests/ms_data_writing_consumer.rs streams a three-spectrum experiment through the consumer and asserts the result is byte-identical to crate::format::mzml::write over the same experiment, and separately reads every streamed document back with mzml::read and compares the records to the input. Both hold, which is what proves the one-record renders are spliced correctly and the index attributes renumbered. The resource ceilings, the duplicate-identifier and undeclared-reference refusals, the CountPolicy choice and the error variants are native decisions (tier 4). No C++ was built or executed and no C++ output was retained, so this is not a tier-1 differential.
gaps: The port does not subclass an mzML handler; it drives crate::format::mzml's whole-document writer once per record and splices the record element out between the list tags. That couples it to three literal tag spellings and to the ' index="0" defaultArrayLength="' marker, all held as constants in the module and all checked - a writer change makes the consumer return Error::Unsupported rather than emit wrong XML. The record-element internals of src/format/mzml* are private to that module, and this package does not own it.

Because of that, every record re-renders the header text and discards it: cost per record is the header plus the record, where the source pays the record only. Memory stays one record at a time, which is the property the class exists for. A future increment that exposes a record-level writer from src/format/mzml would remove the overhead.

A record needing a sourceFileList or dataProcessingList other than the first record's is refused (Error::Unsupported) instead of being written with the dangling reference the source emits. A stream whose records carry differing source files or data-processing histories therefore cannot be written by this port at all; the whole-document writer handles it.
The source parallelises nothing here, but MzMLHandler's binary encoding carries #pragma omp in places; this port is serial throughout, so a large record encodes on one core.

MzMLValidator is not ported: the source constructs one per consumer and passes it to every writer call. The crate's semantic validation is a separate operation behind the mzml-validation feature and is not run per record.
ProgressLogger is a base of the source class and is not threaded through this module.
Indexed mzML output is not offered: the source's writeFooter_ can emit an index from spectra_offsets_/chromatograms_offsets_, which this port does not track. Plain mzML only.

Rust cannot report an error from a drop, so finish() replaces the destructor and dropping a consumer leaves the run and mzML elements unclosed. Documented at the method rather than hidden behind a best-effort Drop that would swallow an I/O failure.
